claims.title: The Xiongnu confederation reaches its height
claims.summary: At the close of the third century BCE the Xiongnu unite the eastern steppe under a supreme chanyu, forming a nomadic empire that rivals the Qin and Han dynasties of China for centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-209bce-the-xiongnu-confederation-reaches-its-height, claim TL:MNG:event:209bce:the-xiongnu-confederation-reaches-its-height, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Break-up of the Xiongnu empire
claims.summary: After prolonged war with China and internal division, the Xiongnu confederation fractures; some tribes are absorbed into China while others scatter, ending the first great steppe empire centred on Mongolia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-48-break-up-of-the-xiongnu-empire, claim TL:MNG:event:48:break-up-of-the-xiongnu-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Uyghur khaganate in the Orkhon valley
claims.summary: Turkic Uyghurs establish a khaganate centred on the Orkhon River, building the city of Khar Balgas; the valley remains the political and ceremonial heart of the eastern steppe.

sources.label: Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape (World Heritage List)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-744-uyghur-khaganate-in-the-orkhon-valley, claim TL:MNG:event:744:uyghur-khaganate-in-the-orkhon-valley, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Temüjin proclaimed Chinggis Khan
claims.summary: An assembly of steppe leaders by the River Onon proclaims Temüjin as Chinggis Khan, 'Universal Ruler,' uniting the Mongol tribes into one nation governed by the Yassa law code, the founding act of the Mongol state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1206-temujin-proclaimed-chinggis-khan, claim TL:MNG:event:1206:temujin-proclaimed-chinggis-khan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conquest of the Khwarazmian empire
claims.summary: Mongol armies invade and destroy the powerful Khwarazmian empire of Central Asia, opening the way to Persia and the Russian steppe and demonstrating the reach of the new Mongol military.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1219-conquest-of-the-khwarazmian-empire, claim TL:MNG:event:1219:conquest-of-the-khwarazmian-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Chinggis Khan
claims.summary: Chinggis Khan dies in August 1227 during a campaign against the Tangut Xixia kingdom, leaving an empire reaching from northern China to the Caspian Sea and a realm divided among his four sons.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1227-death-of-chinggis-khan, claim TL:MNG:event:1227:death-of-chinggis-khan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Karakorum becomes the imperial capital
claims.summary: Great Khan Ögödei walls the city of Karakorum in the Orkhon valley and builds a palace there, establishing a fixed capital for the Mongol Empire on the Mongolian steppe.

sources.label: Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape (World Heritage List)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1235-karakorum-becomes-the-imperial-capital, claim TL:MNG:event:1235:karakorum-becomes-the-imperial-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kublai Khan founds the Yuan dynasty
claims.summary: Chinggis Khan's grandson Kublai proclaims the Yuan dynasty in 1271 and completes the conquest of China by 1279, ruling all of China from Khanbaliq (Beijing) as its first non-Chinese sovereign.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1271-kublai-khan-founds-the-yuan-dynasty, claim TL:MNG:event:1271:kublai-khan-founds-the-yuan-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of the Yuan and retreat to the steppe
claims.summary: The Chinese rebel Zhu Yuanzhang overthrows the Yuan and founds the Ming dynasty; the last Mongol emperor flees north into the steppes, ending Mongol rule over China.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1368-fall-of-the-yuan-and-retreat-to-the-steppe, claim TL:MNG:event:1368:fall-of-the-yuan-and-retreat-to-the-steppe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zanabazar enthroned as first Javzandamba
claims.summary: Zanabazar, recognized as a reincarnation in 1639, is enthroned with the title Javzandamba khutagt, becoming the first Bogd Gegeen and supreme head of Tibetan Buddhism in Mongolia.

sources.label: History of Mongolia: The ascendancy of the Manchu

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1640-zanabazar-enthroned-as-first-javzandamba, claim TL:MNG:event:1640:zanabazar-enthroned-as-first-javzandamba, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Khalkha Mongols submit to the Qing
claims.summary: The Khalkha Mongols of the north accept Manchu overlordship, bringing Mongolia under the Qing dynasty; the Manchus govern through the Mongol nobility and impose religious controls to secure their rule.

sources.label: History of Mongolia: The ascendancy of the Manchu

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1691-khalkha-mongols-submit-to-the-qing, claim TL:MNG:event:1691:khalkha-mongols-submit-to-the-qing, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence declared under the Bogd Khan
claims.summary: As the Qing collapses, Mongolia expels the Manchu official and proclaims the Javzandamba as Bogd Khan, head of an independent theocratic monarchy, though only autonomy under Chinese suzerainty is recognized abroad.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1911-independence-declared-under-the-bogd-khan, claim TL:MNG:event:1911:independence-declared-under-the-bogd-khan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: People's Revolution captures the capital
claims.summary: Damdin Sükhbaatar's People's Army, with the Soviet Red Army, drives out the White Russian forces of Baron Ungern-Sternberg and takes Niislel Khüree in July 1921, installing a people's government.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1921-people-s-revolution-captures-the-capital, claim TL:MNG:event:1921:people-s-revolution-captures-the-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mongolian People's Republic proclaimed
claims.summary: After the death of the Bogd Khan in May 1924, the monarchy lapses and the Mongolian People's Republic is proclaimed in November, the world's second socialist state and a satellite of the Soviet Union.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1924-mongolian-people-s-republic-proclaimed, claim TL:MNG:event:1924:mongolian-people-s-republic-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Great Repression
claims.summary: Under Choibalsan and Soviet NKVD advisers, the state carries out mass purges, killing tens of thousands of people, executing thousands of lamas, and destroying hundreds of Buddhist monasteries.

sources.label: Mongolia: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Mongolia admitted to the United Nations
claims.summary: Mongolia is admitted to the United Nations in 1961, broadening international recognition of its independence after decades in which its sovereignty had been disputed between its powerful neighbours.

sources.label: Mongolia: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Peaceful democratic revolution
claims.summary: Demonstrations and hunger strikes in the capital lead the ruling party's leadership to resign in March 1990, ending one-party communist rule and opening the way to multiparty elections held that year.

sources.label: Mongolia: Reform and the birth of democracy

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1990-peaceful-democratic-revolution, claim TL:MNG:event:1990:peaceful-democratic-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Democratic constitution adopted
claims.summary: A new constitution transforms Mongolia from a people's republic into a multiparty parliamentary democracy with an elected president and the State Great Khural, and commits the country to a market economy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-1992-democratic-constitution-adopted, claim TL:MNG:event:1992:democratic-constitution-adopted, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Oyu Tolgoi and the mining boom
claims.summary: Agreement to develop the giant Oyu Tolgoi copper and gold deposit anchors a mining boom that multiplies Mongolia's income, reorients its economy from herding, and accelerates migration to Ulaanbaatar.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mongolia: From steppe horse-archers to the largest land empire in history, and the long road back to an independent democracy.", terralore.co/country/MNG/chronicle#ev-2009-oyu-tolgoi-and-the-mining-boom, claim TL:MNG:event:2009:oyu-tolgoi-and-the-mining-boom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
